step1_analysis.circuit_type: Transimpedance / Voltage Amplifier with Nonlinear Feedback
step1_analysis.description: A BiCMOS wideband amplifier stage featuring an emitter-follower input, a common-emitter gain stage with emitter degeneration, and an emitter-follower output. It includes a nonlinear feedback path (diode-connected BJT and resistor) to dynamically compress gain at large signal swings, handling a wide dynamic range without saturating.

paper_reference.title: A SiGe BiCMOS Burst-Mode 155-Mb/s Receiver for PON

power_consumption.description: Total DC power dissipation of the amplifier stage.

sky130_expected.calculation: P = VDD * I_total. With VDD=1.8V and estimated bias currents of ~1-2mA total for this single stage.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The paper reports 500mW for the entire receiver chip at 5V. A single gain stage at 1.8V will consume significantly less power.

voltage_gain.description: Midband AC voltage gain from IN to OUT.

sky130_expected.calculation: Gain ~ gm * R_load. For a single stage with R2=1k and gm~40mS, gain is ~32dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The 67dB value is for the full receiver chain. A single stage will provide a fraction of this total gain.

sky130_expected.calculation: BW = 1 / (2*pi*R2*C_total). With R2=1k and C~100fF, BW is ~1.5GHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Modern processes (even using generic BJT models) can easily exceed the 155MHz requirement of the original 2002 paper.

output_swing.description: Peak-to-peak voltage swing at the output.

sky130_expected.calculation: Limited by VDD (1.8V) and VCE(sat) of the BJTs.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The nonlinear feedback compresses the gain at large swings to prevent saturation, limiting the maximum linear swing.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC power, AC voltage gain, -3dB bandwidth, and transient output swing.
step3_testbench.spice:
* SiGe BiCMOS Burst-Mode Receiver Gain Stage
.lib "sky130_fd_pr/models/sky130.lib.spice" tt

* Generic NPN model (used as SKY130 NPNs require specific subcircuit wrappers)
.model npn npn (is=1e-16 bf=100 vaf=50 cjc=100f cje=100f)

.param R1_val=100
.param R2_val=1k
.param CC_val=100f
.param RNLB_val=500
.param RFMB_val=2k
.param IB_val=100u

* DUT
IB VDD N_BIAS {IB_val}
QB0 N_BIAS N_BIAS GND npn
Q1 VDD IN N_Q2B npn
QB1 N_Q2B N_BIAS GND npn
Q2 N_Q2C N_Q2B N_Q2E npn
R1 N_Q2E INDUMMY {R1_val}
R2 VDD N_Q2C {R2_val}
CC VDD N_Q2C {CC_val}
Q3 VDD N_Q2C OUT npn
QB2 OUT N_BIAS GND npn
QNLB N_QNLB N_QNLB N_Q2B npn
RNLB N_QNLB OUT {RNLB_val}
RFMB N_Q2B OUT {RFMB_val}

* Sources
VGND GND 0 0
VVDD VDD GND 1.8
* DC bias adjusted to 1.4V to ensure Q2 turns on properly
VIN IN GND DC 1.4 AC 1 SIN(1.4 0.05 10MEG 0 0)
* INDUMMY set to 0V to provide proper Vbe for Q2
VINDUMMY INDUMMY GND DC 0

.control
* DC Analysis
op
let power = -i(VVDD) * 1.8
print power

* AC Analysis
ac dec 100 1MEG 10G
let gain_db = vdb(OUT)
meas ac midband_gain find gain_db at=10MEG
let gain_db_3db = midband_gain - 3
meas ac bw_3db when gain_db=gain_db_3db fall=1

* Transient Analysis
tran 100p 200n
meas tran vout_pp pp v(OUT)
meas tran vout_max max v(OUT)
meas tran vout_min min v(OUT)

quit
.endc
